title: Production change authorization and forensic logging workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a deterministic, auditable production authorization workflow for model rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) that enforces RBAC, collects immutable forensic logs, supports delegated approvers and emergency 'break-glass' rollback, and surfaces all required sign-offs in the Redwood Console. Rationale: As Dedicated and Private customers adopt more frequent model updates, we need standardized controls so platform, security, and product teams can trust rollouts without manual coordination. Scope: approval policy engine, Console approval UI, approval email/Slack hooks, audit log schema and immutable storage, integration with rollout controller (canary/A-B/shadow), auto-rollback triggers, and retention/exports for compliance teams. Out-of-scope for this ticket: full enterprise SSO onboarding (handled in ENG-2275) and long-term SIEM connectors beyond S3/GCS export (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console: a user can create an approval policy that defines required approvers by role (deployer, security, privacy, product) and by risk tier (minor config, model patch, major model swap)
2) RBAC: approval action is only available to users with Approver role; attempts by non-Approver are rejected and logged

3) Audit logs: each rollout action (create, approve, cancel, complete, rollback) writes an append-only record containing actor, timestamp, model artifact hash, rollout config, metrics snapshot, and signed change-id
4) Auto-rollback: configurable auto-rollback rules can be attached to a rollout (e.g., >3% ERR increase vs baseline OR >5% latency P99 regression) and execute rollback without manual intervention
5) Shadow traffic support: approval policy can be configured to allow shadowing for production traffic without routing user-visible traffic until explicit approval
6) Emergency fast-path: a designated emergency-approver or break-glass token can initiate immediate rollback; action is logged and triggers postmortem workflow
7) Export & retention: audit logs can be exported to S3/GCS with retention policy and encryption via customer KMS
8) E2E test: integration test that simulates a canary, triggers metric regression, and validates auto-rollback execution and audit trail entry
design_notes: Design prefers a two-column approval UI: left column shows policies and required approvers, right column shows rollout preview (model artifact, diff in eval metrics, canary percentage)
For UX, inline rationale is required for approver decisions; make free-text optional but keep a structured 'reason_code' to support audits
We should display a compact 'forensic summary' (actor, action, model hash, metrics delta) next to each rollout timeline entry
security_considerations: Audit logs must be append-only and signed (we will use HSM-backed signing keys managed in KMS)
Audit log access requires Auditor role; raw logs encrypted at rest using customer or company KMS depending on deployment mode
Approval policies that permit auto-approve for low-risk changes must be limited to specific service accounts and require explicit opt-in
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): schema for audit events; minimal Console UI for creating policies; RBAC mapping for Approver role
Phase 2 (week 3-4): integrate approval checks into rollout-controller; attach auto-rollback rules; build e2e test harness
Phase 3 (week 5): shadow traffic support and export to S3/GCS; security review and UX polish; staged canary with internal beta customers
Phase 4 (post-release): SIEM connector, longer retention options, cross-account auditor views
